newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cecchi Gori in TV soccer deal with UFA.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cecchi Gori in TV soccer deal with UFA.

text.p: Media mogul Vittorio Cecchi Gori's television holding said on Thursday it had reached a deal with German satellite TV firm UFA to show World Cup and European soccer championship qualifying matches in Italy.

The deal will include exclusive rights to Italy's crucial match against England at Wembley next February in their qualifying group for the 1998 World Cup in France, Cecchi Gori Communications said in a statement.
The holding operates Cecchi Gori's two television channels, TeleMonteCarlo (TMC) and TMC2. UFA is owned by Germany's Bertelsmann AG.

TMC and TMC2 are competing increasingly with public broadcaster RAI and former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset group, each with three channels, and the soccer deal appeared to be a coup in a country wild on sport.
The statement gave no financial details but described the agreement as a medium to long-term strategic accord.

It said it would cover transmission rights in Italy of a series of "top class soccer events regarding qualifying matches for the 1998 World Cup in France and the 2000 European Championships in Belgium."
The statement said February's England match, which is key to Italy's campaign for the 1998 finals and the first for new national coach Cesare Maldini, would be made available to RAI and Mediaset.
